key_insight: A scalar embedding can compress neural network training dynamics into a low-dimensional trajectory while still preserving key behaviors such as sensitivity to initial conditions and Lyapunov-exponent estimates.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical visualization and analysis tool for diagnosing optimization dynamics in large neural networks without needing to inspect the full high-dimensional parameter space.
method: Treat training trajectories as temporal networks and embed them into a scalar time series.
Train a multilayer perceptron on MNIST and compare dynamics in original versus embedded spaces.
Use embedded trajectory statistics to estimate decorrelation time and analyze asymptotic spacing distributions.
evidence_signal: On MNIST, the embedding reproduces main dynamical features of the original parameter space, including regime-dependent sensitivity and an accurate reconstruction of the maximum Lyapunov exponent.
watch_item: The approach is validated on one model and dataset, so its robustness across architectures, tasks, and optimizers remains to be established.
paper_title: Scalar Representations of Neural Network Training Dynamics
